old_claims.statement: The conjugate-linear bundle-metric Serre star transfers closed domains, exactness, closed ranges and minimal inverse norms from E^*-valued (m,*) forms with multiplier h to the reversed E-valued (0,*) complex with multiplier h^(-1).
old_claims.attribution: Standard L2 bundle-dual star/domain duality; original manuscript transfer expanded by old Argus proof.md Section 6. Manifold domain statements are supported by Chakrabarti--Shaw arxiv:1006.3117v2; the orbifold specialization is the draft's local argument.
old_claims.supported_scope: The specified complete orbifold complex with the full reciprocal bundle metric, not arbitrary incomplete domains or unconditioned closed-form solvability.

supported_scope: The full coefficient metric and its reciprocal make J_h an anti-isometry on complementary degrees and dual bundles.
Maximal/minimal source identities become the asserted complete-domain identities after the separately justified core argument.
Exactness of the closed-range adjoint complex, including the endpoint kernel statement.
Equality of reduced inverse norms and no loss in the quantitative constants.
Finite invariant-chart extension supplied by the draft rather than attributed to a manifold theorem.

citation_assessment.terminology_qualification: Adjoint of minimal Dolbeault means the maximal formal adjoint, not the minimal realization of the formal adjoint.

limitations: The primary paper states manifold results, not this orbifold extension.
Minimal and maximal domains are not identified on general incomplete manifolds.
Completeness does not supply closed range or exactness without the other hypotheses.
General source solvability retains range/annihilator conditions.
The scalar Lean formalization does not certify this domain transfer.

prior_review_reconciliation.interpretation: Historical same-subject prose support; current native acceptance is not inherited.

decisive_checks: The local coefficient transformation has norm |G*conjugate(f)|^2/G=G*|f|^2.
The source proposition distinguishes the two maximal/minimal-adjoint pairings.
Exactness of the reversed adjoint complex follows from orthogonal complements and closed range.
Reduced inverse operators are Hilbert adjoints and conjugate isometries preserve their norms.
